epithet: Out of darknesses, into the light
lede: “A Book We have sent down to you, that you may bring mankind out of darknesses into the light.” That is its first sentence and its whole subject. It gathers the messengers into one voice and their peoples into another — and then goes to the valley of Makkah, where an old man stands by a house with no crops round it and prays for those who will live there.

names.name: Ibrāhīm
names.note: After the prayer of Ibrāhīm for Makkah and for his descendants (14:35–41), which is the heart of the surah.

revelation.detail: Ibn al-Jawzī says it is Makkan without any disagreement he knew of, except that Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatādah set apart two ayat: “Have you not seen those who exchanged the favour of Allah for ingratitude…” and the one after it (14:28–29). Al-Qurṭubī explains that these were said to have come down about the idolaters who fought at Badr. Ibn ʿAbbās’s own words, in al-Bukhārī, are that they are the disbelievers of the people of Makkah. The traditional order places the surah seventy-second.

evidence.quote: وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ مِن غَيْرِ خِلافٍ عَلِمْناهُ بَيْنَهم، إلّا ما رُوِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، وقَتادَةَ أنَّهُما قالا: سِوى آيَتَيْنِ مِنها
مَكِّيَّةٌ كُلُّهَا فِي قَوْلِ الْحَسَنِ وَعِكْرِمَةَ وَجَابِرٍ

setting: Ibn Kathīr, at its opening, notes how wide the commission is: the noblest Book, sent down to the noblest messenger, for all the people of the earth, Arab and non-Arab. The surah is addressed to Quraysh, but it speaks of “mankind” in its first ayah and its last.

Having said what the Prophet ﷺ was sent to do, it shows that the task is not new. Mūsā was told the same: “Bring your people out of darknesses into the light, and remind them of the days of Allah.” And then, instead of telling the stories of the prophets one by one as other surahs do, it runs them together. All the messengers speak as one: “Is there any doubt about Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth?” All the peoples answer as one: “You are only human beings like us.” — “We are indeed only human beings like you; but Allah bestows His favour on whom He wills of His servants.” — “We shall drive you out of our land, unless you return to our religion.” Quraysh were about to say that last sentence themselves.

It is a surah of images. The deeds of those who deny their Lord are like ashes on which the wind blows hard on a stormy day. A good word is like a good tree: its root firm, its branches in the sky, giving its fruit in every season. A bad word is like a bad tree, torn up from the surface of the earth, with nothing to hold it. And on the Day of Judgement Satan himself rises to address those who followed him: “Allah made you a promise of truth; I made you a promise, and broke it. I had no power over you, except that I called you, and you answered. So do not blame me; blame yourselves.”

Then it turns to the city where all this was being recited. “Have you not seen those who exchanged the favour of Allah for ingratitude, and settled their people in the abode of ruin?” What favour? The surah answers by going back to the day the place was founded. “My Lord, make this land secure, and keep me and my sons from worshipping idols… Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in a valley without crops, by Your Sacred House — our Lord, that they may keep up the prayer. So make the hearts of people incline towards them, and provide them with fruits, that they may give thanks.” The people of Makkah lived, every day, inside the answer to that prayer. The one thing it asked of them in return was the thing they had abandoned.
aim: To set out the task of the messengers, and their eagerness to bring people out of the darknesses of idolatry into the light of tawḥīd, against the turning away of their peoples — to steady the Prophet ﷺ, and to warn the wrongdoers.
themes: Every messenger in his people’s tongue
“If you give thanks, I will increase you”
The good word and the good tree

outline.title: The commission
outline.summary: Alif Lām Rā. A Book We have sent down to you, that you may bring mankind out of darknesses into the light, by their Lord’s leave, to the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy. We sent no messenger but in the language of his people, to make things clear to them. We sent Mūsā with Our signs: “Bring your people out of darknesses into the light, and remind them of the days of Allah.” Your Lord proclaimed: “If you give thanks, I will surely increase you; and if you are ungrateful, My punishment is severe.”

outline.title: The messengers and their peoples
outline.summary: Has there not come to you the news of those before you — the people of Nūḥ, ʿĀd, Thamūd, and those after them? Their messengers said: “Is there any doubt about Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth?” They said: “You are only human beings like us.” Those who disbelieved said to their messengers: “We shall drive you out of our land.” Their Lord revealed: “We shall destroy the wrongdoers, and settle you in the land after them.” The deeds of those who deny their Lord are like ashes on which the wind blows hard on a stormy day.

outline.title: Satan’s speech, and the two trees
outline.summary: They will all come forth before Allah, and the weak will say to those who were arrogant: “We were your followers.” And Satan will say, when the matter is decided: “Allah made you a promise of truth; I promised you, and failed you. Do not blame me; blame yourselves.” Have you not seen how Allah sets out a likeness: a good word is like a good tree, its root firm and its branches in the sky. And a bad word is like a bad tree, uprooted from the earth. Allah keeps firm those who believe, with the firm word, in the life of this world and in the next.

outline.title: Favour exchanged for ingratitude
outline.summary: Have you not seen those who exchanged the favour of Allah for ingratitude, and settled their people in the abode of ruin? Tell My servants who believe to keep up the prayer and to spend, before a Day comes in which there is no bargaining and no friendship. Allah is He who created the heavens and the earth, sent down water, and brought out fruits; who subjected to you the ships, the rivers, the sun and the moon, the night and the day. He gave you of all that you asked of Him. If you count the favours of Allah, you cannot number them.

outline.title: The prayer of Ibrāhīm
outline.summary: When Ibrāhīm said: “My Lord, make this land secure, and keep me and my sons from worshipping idols. Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in a valley without crops, by Your Sacred House. Praise be to Allah, who has given me, in old age, Ismāʿīl and Isḥāq. My Lord, make me one who keeps up the prayer, and of my descendants too. Our Lord, forgive me, and my parents, and the believers, on the Day the reckoning is set up.”

outline.title: The Day the earth is changed
outline.summary: Do not think Allah unaware of what the wrongdoers do; He only gives them respite until a Day when eyes will stare. Warn people of the Day the punishment comes, and they say: “Our Lord, give us respite for a short while.” They plotted their plot — though their plot were such as to move mountains. The Day the earth is changed to another earth, and the heavens. This is a message for mankind, that they may be warned by it, and know that He is One God.

keyAyah.why: The surah’s own statement of what the Book is for; everything after it shows that purpose carried out, resisted, and prayed for.

virtues.text: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he said: “Tell me of a tree that is like the Muslim: its leaves do not fall, and it gives its fruit at every season.” Ibn ʿUmar said: “It came to my mind that it was the date-palm; but I saw that Abū Bakr and ʿUmar did not speak, and I was shy to.” When they said nothing, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “It is the date-palm.”

“When the Muslim is questioned in the grave, he bears witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah. That is His saying: ‘Allah keeps firm those who believe, with the firm word, in the life of this world and in the next.’”
virtues.arabic: الْمُسْلِمُ إِذَا سُئِلَ فِي الْقَبْرِ يَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ

virtues.text: ʿĀʾishah said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about His saying, “The Day the earth is changed to another earth, and the heavens” — “Where will the people be that Day, Messenger of Allah?” He said: “On the Bridge.”
Ibn ʿAbbās said of “those who exchanged the favour of Allah for ingratitude”: “They are the disbelievers of the people of Makkah.”

before: Al-Raʿd ended with the disbelievers’ verdict: “You are not a messenger.” Sūrat Ibrāhīm begins with Allah’s: a Book sent down to you, to bring mankind into the light.
after: Sūrat Ibrāhīm ends: “This is a message for mankind.” Al-Ḥijr opens with what will become of those who refuse it: “Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they had been Muslims.”
